query: drug shortage product substitution medication error rate hospital incident reports pharmacy intervention log
synthesis: The recorded search returned nothing. From general knowledge, four leads may be worth checking: a national survey of pharmacists on shortage-related errors, a paediatric study of concentration changes, a consensus definition, and a case series on potassium substitutions. None has been retrieved or read.

items.title: Medication errors associated with drug shortages: a national survey of hospital pharmacists
items.keyFindings: Most responding pharmacists reported at least one shortage-related error in the previous year, most often involving dose or concentration.

items.title: Concentration changes during shortages and dosing errors in paediatric inpatients
items.keyFindings: Dosing errors rose after an oral solution concentration change until labels were revised.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; no year or quality rating available.

items.title: Defining shortage-related medication errors: a consensus statement
items.keyFindings: Defines a shortage-related error as one in which the substituted product, its concentration or its preparation contributed.

items.title: Intravenous potassium product substitution and hyperkalaemia events: a case series
items.keyFindings: Five hyperkalaemia events followed a switch to a more concentrated potassium product.

summary: Four unchecked leads after an empty search.
